meta.dataset: Week 10 (2026) personnel-deficiency tracker — starters vs 2nd/3rd/4th string
meta.what_this_is: A cross-tab of the official Week 10 injury report against the club's own published depth chart, so that 'a starter is out' can be distinguished from 'a 4th-string player is out'. Two official sources, one join.

sources.depth_chart_policy: Club-published 'Unofficial Depth Chart'. Every NFL club's own site publishes one; NFL.com's own depth-chart route returns 404 (verified).

meta.depth_hierarchy_rule: Depth position = the 1-based column in which the club lists the player for that position group. Column 1 = starter (1st string), column 2 = 2nd string, column 3 = 3rd string, column 4 = 4th string. A player listed in a group but not in the injury report is depth information only, not a deficiency.
meta.critical_caveat: A club depth chart is explicitly labelled UNOFFICIAL by every club that publishes one. It is the organisation's own working document, not a league-mandated designation. It can lag a coaching decision. This is stated on the site and is the single biggest limitation of this analysis.
meta.coverage: 4 clubs have a verified depth chart transcribed in this dataset (KC, GB, NE, DET). For the other 28 clubs the injury rows are published with depth_position = null and are flagged as 'depth unmapped' rather than guessed. See Flagged for Review FL-10.
meta.not_charted_reason: Transcribing and verifying 32 club depth charts line by line is beyond this session's verified budget. Publishing 28 unverified charts would violate the no-inference rule, so they are left explicitly blank.
meta.unique_group_keys: Every position group key is unique inside its side. This was added after a verification run showed duplicate 'DT'/'CB' labels causing a 3rd-string player to be scored as a starter.
meta.verification: scripts/verify_personnel.py re-derives every depth slot from this file and asserts no player occupies two different slots in the same club chart.

chart_corrections: The Chiefs chart's LT row names 'Kahlil Benson'; the NFL.com roster also lists a Kahlil Benson. Two different players can appear under one name, so the LT STARTER slot is left unasserted rather than guessed. Only the 2nd-string LT (Diego Pounds) is asserted.
The KC chart's DE/DT rows are printed with two labels each reading DT and two reading DE. Group keys here are disambiguated (DT_L/DT_R) to prevent a depth slot being read off the wrong row.

GB.label_as_published: Green Bay Packers Depth Chart (Unofficial, Nov. 10, 2026)
chart_corrections: Two DT, two EDGE, two LB and two CB rows are printed with identical labels. Group keys are disambiguated so a depth slot can only be read off the row it actually appears in.

NE.label_as_published: Patriots Unofficial Depth Chart (published by Patriots.com writers, not the organisation)
chart_corrections: Three DT rows share one label; disambiguated as DT_1/DT_2/DT_3.

DET.label_as_published: 2026 Unofficial Depth Chart Compiled by Lions Football Communications
chart_corrections: Two EDGE, two DL, three LB and two CB/S rows share labels; disambiguated.
